reason: Audit (reports/paper/hllag_forward_audit.md): the container clock runs ~2.8 s behind real time and drifts ~-0.33 s/h. sim_lag compares our local Binance receive time with HL exchange timestamps, so forward entries were filled at HL quotes received 1.4-2.0 s BEFORE the signal (look-ahead in our favour). In the Tardis backtest HL quotes were received +130..340 ms after their exchange time.
change: At scoring time only, HL quotes/trades get timestamp := local_timestamp - 175 ms (the backtest relation). hlanchor_lib.py (frozen sha256) and the frozen params are unchanged; the raw chunks are unchanged.
scope: Applies retroactively to ALL forward trades since each freeze, including the 5 already scored under the old stamping (which were profitable under the flawed stamping and lose under this one). The old ledgers are kept as *_ledger_unamended.json for the record.
known_remaining_risks: fill at next HL quote change after latency, not verified against displayed size (no depth recorded)
collector stalls ~0.5-1.2 s once per hour while writing chunks
35 s gap at 05:47 and ~1 min at 07:22 from restarts
our real order latency to HL is ~0.3-0.45 s after signal, close to the profit/loss flip
decided_before_seeing: Decided after the audit showed that the 5 trades lose under re-alignment; the amendment makes the score stricter, never looser, and applies to all trades.

amendment_2.change: Drop all rows with local_timestamp in [2026-10-05 07:25:40, 07:26:45) local clock from every stream at scoring (treated as a gap). Cause: a 72 s test run of the collector (to check a flush fix) appended a duplicate stream into the live hour-07 chunk files. Scores were identical with and without the exclusion (dev 3 / -20.58, newcoins 2 / -3.23, addendum 0), so no trade was affected.
amendment_2.collector_changes_2026-10-05: chunk writes moved off the event loop (worker thread + lock) to remove ~0.5-1.2 s hourly stalls; Binance event_time_ms recorded as an extra column (unused by sim_lag). Takes effect at the next collector restart.
